GTA 6 Launch Stats Are In: Over 50% Of Active Console People Played

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (352 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has already outgrossed the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, the highest-grossing movie in history — and the sheer scale of that success is represented in the launch day stats.
  • According to Mat Piscatella, senior director and video game industry advisor at Circana, over 50% of all active consoler consumers played GTA 6 at launch, averaging 494–513 minutes of playtime, or roughly 8 hours.
  • That does not mean 50% of all console consumers played it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has already outgrossed the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, the highest-grossing movie in history — and the sheer scale of that success is represented in the launch day stats.

According to Mat Piscatella, senior director and video game industry advisor at Circana, over 50% of all active consoler consumers played GTA 6 at launch, averaging 494–513 minutes of playtime, or roughly 8 hours.

That does not mean 50% of all console consumers played it.

Sources indicate that "For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6," he posted to Bluesky. "PS5 GTA 6 players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494. Both the DAU and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers.".

Piscatella doesn't have the exact stats to hand, explaining that it's "not exactly easy to go back and sort daily active engagement rates," but to his recollection, during his time at Circana, there has been "nothing near this.".

According to recent reports, the only game second to GTA 6 on launch was Fortnite, accounting for 10% of all active players across both platforms. Clearly, the Pirate Shop Access tokens are working.

As for what GTA 6 players were up to before the game released, Piscatella had some additional stats, sharing the top-five games between November 6 and 19:.

$3.7 billion in revenue within 24 hours, "the biggest entertainment launch of all time," accounting for over 50% of all active console users — those numbers are nothing to scoff at.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, in less than a week, with 32.5 million copies sold, GTA 6 is already one of the best-selling games of all-time. It right now sits on the edge of the top 30 after overtaking Super Mario Odyssey, Borderlands 2, and Monster Hunter: World.

Considering that GTA 5 is the third best-selling game of all-time, behind only Minecraft and Tetris (clearly, the secret to selling hundreds of millions of copies is blocks), it's easy to imagine GTA 6 landing somewhere near the top.

Avoiding Steam Machine this Black Friday? Here's what other mini PCs can actually get you for your cash

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a latest system.
  • That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in.
  • These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a latest system.

That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in. Whether you want more options further down the price range or you're after something with more graphical grunt, these compact PCs prove it's not just Valve producing ready-to-go gaming machines that don't take up floor space.

These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.

In a recent development, I've spent the last few months road-testing mini PCs from Geekom to Asus, spanning the full price range. Right at the bottom, boxes like the $499 Geekom A5 2027 Edition will gear themselves heavily towards indie titles and retro emulation. At the top, you'll find full dedicated GPU options spanning up to the RTX 5070.

It's worth noting that the Windows operating system won't give you that living-room-console ease of the Steam Machine, but instead opens you up to more versatility around launchers and OS compatibility.

Like you, I was curious to see what these tiny little rigs could actually conjure - and you'll find out exactly how each price point fared in my benchmarks just below.

In a recent development, I've spent the last six months running my everyday workflow through mini PCs across a range of brands, testing every compact rig I can get my hands on in whatever games they allow for. Around that, I've also been testing and reviewing gaming laptops on GamesRadar+ for the last six years, using similar components in different configurations every two weeks.

In a recent development, the best deal you'll find on the budget Geekom A5 2027 Edition right now sits with Amazon. A $50 discount on the original $549 takes us to $499 this Black Friday. While prices have been jumping since the start of the year here, that's cheaper than it has been since July. This one's dropped to around $400 earlier in 2026, though.

According to recent reports, the Geekom A5 2027 Edition is a productivity machine first and foremost. The AMD Ryzen 7 7730U under the hood is designed to run efficiently, quietly, and with minimal power draw. That means it can hum away in the background without breaking the bank, but it also sweeps away a lot of the power more demanding games require.

I was still curious to see how gaming actually fares at the lower end of the budget. In short, this thing will run your indie Steam library no problem. If you prioritize smaller titles, you'll get on just fine here and likely kick yourself if you opt for anything more expensive. Retro emulation runs nicely as well, if that's your jam.

In a recent development, that's about as far as you'll get, though. Shadow of the Tomb Raider, an older "double-A" release that doesn't tend to make too many gaming laptops sweat, neared smooth framerates only with resolution set to 720p and settings dropped to their lowest. Medium can just about squeak by on a smaller screen at 28fps.

The same story is true of Cyberpunk 2077, the massive guns test. Without frame generation you're looking at 27fps at 720p here, though we do jump up nicely to 45fps with a little extra help.

These more demanding games are playable. They run. You can even get over 30fps if you make larger sacrifices - a perfectly decent position at the budget end of the spectrum. They're just not going to feel nearly as good as they might slightly further up the price scale.

Recent findings suggest that the GMKTec K8 Plus has dropped under $700 in the past, but today's $170 discount is a starting point. I'd keep a close eye on this one as Black Friday progresses, rather than diving in straight away now - this one stands to wriggle under that $700 threshold if we're lucky.

The GMKTec K8 Plus upgrades your processor to the Ryzen 7 8845HS, adds an Oculink connection for future eGPU upgrades, and includes extra support for more monitor displays. That's a set of upgrades that will set you up for more demanding games a lot better than the budget-minded Geekom A5.

It has been revealed that in practice, that means solid 40+fps in Shadow of the Tomb Raider at both medium and high settings in 1080p, with Cyberpunk 2077 managing 41fps in medium as well. You've got a lot more breathing room here, as well as power ceiling that allows for that FHD resolution.

Mid-range "double-As" are more-than possible with a few tweaks, and more demanding titles are within reach here as well.

Sources indicate that ultimately, this is your all-rounder. It's powerful enough to represent solid value for money across chunkier games while still giving you room to grow with that eGPU connection and easily upgradeable innards.

In a recent development, I have one major caveat from my testing, though. You might need to upgrade the Wi-Fi card when you buy it. Internet was incredibly slow for me during testing, far slower than any other device on my network. There's something funky going on behind the scenes here, but people have reported a fresh card solves the problem.

The Geekom A9 Max is available with that Ryzen Ai 9 HX470 chipset, 2TB SSD and 32GB RAM for $1,499. Again this one has been cheaper this year so far, so it's worth watching over the next week. Still, it's been locked in at $1600 since August.

The Geekom A9 Max is a step up in price compared to our more budget-friendly alternatives, and overtakes the 2TB Steam Machine cost. So what's in it for you?

This is actually a very similar value proposition to the Steam Machine, hitting 30+fps in Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p Medium settings without any frame generation help. Adding frame-gen into the equation, and it's easy to speed well past that 60fps threshold. It's a step up where more demanding games like CD Projekt Red's open world are concerned, though improvements further down the scale are more measured compared to the GMKTec further up.

Industry observers note that what's going to separate these two rigs, though, is what else you want to do with your PC. The Geekom A9 Max can match the Steam Machine in overall performance, but it also adds a whole workstation into your purchase.

It has been revealed that this is where Windows plays its most notable card in this trip into mini PC land. While you won't have that console-like operating system, you'll have everything you need for demanding productivity tasks and workflows on top of that gaming performance. It's the better option for those not just buying a gaming device, but rolling their purchase in with their work machine.

We're down to a brand-upcoming record-low price on the RTX 5070 Asus ROG GR70 mini PC this Black Friday, with the $2,599 configuration shedding $300 from the final price. This one's only ever dipped just below $2,500 in previous sales, though it's still one of the most expensive mini PCs on the market.

The largest, and most expensive, mini PC I've had on my test bench so far, the Asus ROG GR70 isn't a budget alternative to the Steam Machine but an additional investment in more demanding PC games. This is a full system, with a dedicated RTX 5070 graphics card humming away inside, and some of AMD's most powerful processors up top as well.

I tested the AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D / RTX 5070 version with a whopping 64GB RAM under the hood. That's a particularly expensive configuration in today's rates, one that comes in at around $2,800.

For that kind of cash, you can easily pick up one of the best gaming laptops or a cheaper full-tower PC - so the ROG GR70 is only for those specifically seeking a miniature form factor.

How did it go? Unsurprisingly, for a rig often twice the price of the Steam Machine, pretty damn smoothly. Triple-figure frame rates are the norm for most Triple-As in high settings at FHD, while we're still well above 60fps in everything at 1440p as well.

That's performance that's going to blow the Steam Machine out the water, but it's still tracking behind other RTX 5070 counterparts. The value of this beast compared to an RTX 5070 gaming laptop or desktop PC doesn't quite stack up - you'll need to know you're in it for the miniature footprint for this premium pick to make sense.

We're also rounding up the best gaming handhelds and best gaming tablets for more ways to play this holiday season.

Managing Editor of Hardware at GamesRadar+, I originally landed in hardware at our sister site TechRadar before moving over to GamesRadar. In between, I've written for Tom’s Guide, Wireframe, The Indie Game Website and That Video Game Blog, covering everything from the PS5 launch to the Apple Pencil. Now, i'm focused on Nintendo Switch, gaming laptops (and the keyboards, headsets and mice that come with them), PS5, and trying to find the perfect projector.

Latest Update: Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.
  • Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.
  • This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.

Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.

This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.

Digital Foundry reckons that the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 is a great-looking game for the most part, highlighting things like lighting, reflections and even the incredible hair system, while also pointing out minor downsides such as missing shadows and occasionally blurry appearances. They also reckon that the frame rate generally maintains its 30FPS target, but will slip in busy situations like chases and explosions.

"Generally speaking, the game acquits itself quite well on Microsoft's senior current-gen console. Visual settings seem pretty solid across the board.".

The Xbox Series S version is also noted to be pretty good in the graphical department, retaining the core features that make GTA 6 such a great game visually. It's the frame rate that bothers DF the most, as it's much more variable and prone to falling below its 30FPS target. That said, it appears to hover around 25-30FPS for the most part.

"Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.".

Recent findings suggest that if you're wondering which console is the absolute best to play GTA 6 on, it's unsurprisingly the PS5 Pro. Nevertheless, Digital Foundry indicates that both the Xbox Series X and the PS5 versions "look and play well" despite their softer image (and the Series X is actually "slightly smoother" when setting the Xbox to 120Hz with a VRR display), while the Xbox Series S version is the "hardest to recommend" despite its surprisingly impressive visuals.

Recent findings suggest that "In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.".

Both the video and the website article are totally different from each other, so it's worth watching / reading the pair of them and getting a better idea of how GTA 6 fares across both Xbox consoles (and PS5 for that matter).

In my experience, I've found GTA 6 to be fantastic on Xbox Series X across the board for the most part, and while the Series S version is clearly a little more unstable, I'd wager that most players will still be perfectly happy with it.

Sources indicate that what are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Breaking: GTA 6 is playable in first-person, here's how to activate it

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (451 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that while you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode.
  • Sources indicate that it's easy enough to activate in-game.
  • In a recent development, as Morgan's footage indicates, it's completely playable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

Sources indicate that it's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then swiftly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

In a recent development, as Morgan's footage indicates, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future patch.

If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.

#86373. GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (414 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks.
  • It has been revealed that not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it.
  • Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks. What began with ramming a dump truck into it swiftly spiraled into spawning 100 rhino tanks, placing a UFO on the tracks, or even flooding Los Santos with a tsunami. Nothing worked. So, when GTA 6 finally hit store shelves, the number one question people raced to answer was: can you stop the train?

It has been revealed that not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it. As shown by Twitter user jax_caine (video embedded below), the train isn't an unstoppable force of nature anymore. Hitting it from the side causes it to swerve off the rails, and if you wait around for another train, the two will collide.

Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.

If you stand on the tracks, a train will brake before hitting you. Likewise, when the train sees another train blocking the tracks, rather than ramming into it at full speed and causing a massive pile-up, it'll slow down. Hell, if you put a body on the tracks, they stop and even sound their horn at you.

GTA 5's trains worked a little differently. They're static objects and their position is updated through coordinates, independent of physics interactions, which means that instead of reacting to the game's physics engine, they follow hard-coded tracks and override anything in their way. That's why they turn into submersibles when you flood Los Santos, and easily tear through 100 tanks. They literally can't be stopped.

We don't know exactly how they work in GTA 6 yet, but it's clear they aren't static objects anymore. They behave like other vehicles, reacting dynamically to the world. You could fly a plane into the train and it'd be thrown off course, rather than bravely continuing ahead without a scratch.

Still, even with GTA 6 in hand and a train that we can derail, I doubt that'll stop the community from finding increasingly elaborate ways to stop the freight train. Even if they never do. With that mystery out of the way, maybe we can turn our attention to those strange symbols near Manifest Canyon, eh?

Sources indicate that in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Industry observers note that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Recent findings suggest that version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Sources indicate that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

Sources indicate that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a upcoming game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent organization Microsoft are still right now subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Not only bring those games back, but bundle them together.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie. A legitimately great 3D platformer that also immerses fans of the films in its world in ways that not many other tie-in games have ever managed to pull off. That’s why those of us who played it when it originally released were thrilled to find out it was part of Digital Eclipse’s surprising effort to bring pretty much all past Toy Story games to modern platforms.

Not only bring those games back, but bundle them together. The Retro Roundup, which combines all of the older games from the ‘90s and early ‘00s into one collection, and a remaster of Toy Story 3 for modern platforms. Best of all, the Roundup and the remaster can be bought as part of the same bundle, not just digitally, but physically, too.

Sources indicate that for decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace. Almost expected, particularly for the bigger Disney blockbusters. Aladdin, Hercules, Tarzan - they all had games that were released alongside their movies, giving fans another way to experience what they had just seen on the massive screen.

Sources indicate that that tradition has all but died out for several reasons. Trying to release a game and a movie at the same time is no longer possible, largely due to how long it takes to make games that would be considered worthy of big-budget blockbusters. Even if a developer were to hit the ground running the second the mere idea for a movie was uttered, that movie would still end up getting made long before the game was even close to being finished, likely by a margin of years.

It’s why Toy Story 3 was probably one of the last true movie tie-in games we will ever get, which is somewhat ironic as it’s also one of the best. The trouble is, especially now with the release of its remaster, people are looking back on it and longing for another era where movies can have tie-in games released alongside them. It’s not the feeling of long-lost nostalgia we should be focusing on when playing this remaster, though. Developers and movie studios should be looking at what Disney and Avalanche did with that original game, what Digital Eclipse has done with the remaster, and using all of that as the blueprint for the future of movie games.

Industry observers note that even though the Toy Story 3 game and movie were released at the same time, the former isn’t just a game version of the latter. It’s effectively a love letter to the entire series, or at least the original trilogy, that pulls from those first three beloved movies. Its developers were given more freedom, which is how we wound up with the more open Woody’s Roundup area, one of the - if not the - main reasons the game was so popular.

According to recent reports, the game didn’t need to release alongside the movie to be a success, something its Complete Edition has now proved 16 years later. Those who played the original have been reminded of just how good it was, and how it told a separate Toy Story story while remaining faithful to the films, and Disney now has a shiny new polished version to point new, younger fans towards not just when a new Toy Story movie is released, but whenever they need to.

Industry observers note that that’s the lesson that other studios which have all-but given up on movie games really need to try and learn from. That you don’t need to pull off the almost-impossible and try to get the launch of a movie and its game to perfectly align. What’s more vital is making sure that game is good and can stand the test of time. If so, you can not only release it whenever, but whenever you need it again, you have something to point to. Or, if it’s been long enough, you can give it the remaster treatment like Toy Story 3.

Recent findings suggest that I wouldn’t even be averse to seeing Toy Story 3 dusted off and remastered a second time a decade from now, perhaps to give Toy Story fans who haven’t even been born yet something to play two console generations from now when the sixth, seventh, and eighth movies are released. Add an extra area to Woody’s Roundup. Throw in a few more story missions. It’s certainly a lot easier than making a whole new game from scratch, which is the problem that has effectively ended the movie video game era.

I appreciate that “Hey, just make a game that’s as good as Toy Story 3 and you’ll be set for life” is easier noted than done. The thing is, I don’t think anyone is even trying. Just look at the excitement surrounding the reveal of the Coco world in Kingdom Hearts 4. There’s a Coco sequel coming, and a game like Toy Story 3 set in that world could be huge, even if it doesn’t line up with the release of its sequel. Sadly, I think Coco’s inclusion in KH is the closest we’ll ever get to a video game set in Disney’s Land of the Dead.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300.
  • By the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, which is the much easier way to get in. If you'd still rather unlock the safe the classic way, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

By the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

You'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

You'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Fortunately, there are some sticky bombs conveniently stashed in the next room, meaning it's the much safer option that heading out to the boatworks.

We previously believed this option required reaching one of the Chapter 3 GTA 6 missions, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, but with the few explosives available in the bowling alley, you're golden. Keep the spares on you, and you can use them to get into other safes around Leonida, too.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously.
  • But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski.
  • In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our newly introduced galactic overlords!".

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Sources indicate that offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is at the moment none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that with Nintendo launching its Black Friday sale on the European eShop earlier this week, we knew it was only a matter of time before our friends in North America got some savings of their own. And what do you know, they have!

In a recent development, nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' sale is now live on the North American storefront, with discounts across a bunch of first- and third-party delights. It'll be sticking around until 2nd December at 11:59pm PT, so you still have a couple of weeks to make the most of it.

In a recent development, just like with the EU sale, we have assembled the following list of every game in the Adventure Awaits offer that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick from the 8/10s at the end, because we couldn't see it go unmentioned.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

In a recent development, please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

According to recent reports, this excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

Sources indicate that the Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

According to recent reports, difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

Sources indicate that BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

It has been revealed that card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre swiftly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

It has been revealed that catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent latest character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface challenges which are easily ignored.

According to recent reports, at roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

Sources indicate that there isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

Recent findings suggest that along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in said education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Recent findings suggest that every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This newly introduced release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Sources indicate that granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

According to recent reports, invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

In a recent development, easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great substantial colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole big bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the new transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

Industry observers note that one of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful fresh content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

Industry observers note that with a bunch of fantastic latest abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great major boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

According to recent reports, that latest upgrade was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page at the moment indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of concerns.

Sources indicate that "We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there presently looks to have been no major hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

Rob Run Is Surging On Steam As PC Players Look For A GTA 6 Alternative

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months.
  • Rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," rolled out on Steam earlier this month.
  • On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months. However, one game is already filling the void.

Rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," rolled out on Steam earlier this month. It was a pretty successful release for Last Day on Earth and Frostborn developer Kefir, with a 23,000 peak on November 4 rising to 43,000 within just a few days — a number that only skyrocketed as GTA 6 got closer and closer.

On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.

To put those numbers into perspective, it's the fourth most-played game on the platform right now, competing with heavy-hitters like CS2 and Apex Legends:.

According to recent reports, admittedly, Rob Run is closer to something like GTA Online (specifically, RP) than GTA 6, but it has all the hallmarks: bank robberies, police chases, convenience store stick-ups, and the rags-to-riches criminal enterprise story that defines so many Grand Theft Auto games. "In just one week, you can go from being a regular thug to the boss of the server's largest organization," the description reads. "And then start over — with new experience, allies, and a more ambitious blueprint to seize power.".

It has been revealed that it sounds like a solid alternative to GTA 6 on paper, even if it doesn't quite measure up to the charm of NotGTAV, the Snake-like parody where you drive around in a Tesco car park that kept us going while we waited for Los Santos, but there's a substantial asterisk here. Developer Kefir admits to using AI "in the creation of certain graphic elements," and the 'Mixed' reviews paint a stark picture of cheaters running rampant and a completely unwelcoming community that have made the game impenetrable for newcomers.

"Half enjoyable AI slop rendered completely unplayable due to the worst cheating crisis I've seen since Counter-Strike," reads one review.

"Great concept, ruined by the community," says another. "Cops just kill on sight (KOS) the moment they see you wearing a mask. Criminals aren't any better. Both sides constantly camp selling areas and extraction points, making it almost pointless to even try playing the game as intended.".

Sources indicate that "Every store you try to rob is already robbed or you get shot by another player just getting out of your car," warns one reviewer. "Tried to live an honest life and play as a cop but everyone is already playing as a cop so it will not let you. As a upcoming player, all I could do is drive around and return to Lenny's cause any time I slowed down I got rammed by some other robber.".

Plenty of reviews raise eyebrows that AI appears to have been used more than the disclosure lets on, while complaining of connection concerns and long maintenance windows interrupting the experience. Kefir is already working to address some of these problems, adding a more overt report button, improving servers, and limiting voice chat to target toxicity, while also adding more methods to detect cheaters, but the negative reviews only continue to pour in.

In a recent development, "I've never experienced this many hackers in a game before," a review from earlier today claimed. "Within 30 minutes of a server going live, people are already using aimbot and pulling bank heists. Servers not being region locked makes things even worse. The game is also practically unplayable for solo players. Winning a 1v2 is possible, but a 1v3 is impossible [...] The game is fun and has potential, but between hackers, camping, and the huge advantage groups have over solo players, it's honestly more frustrating than enjoyable. Not worth the headache in its current state.".

So, while it might be a solid free-to-play alternative to GTA 6 right now, the reality of Rob Run is a game plagued by overt AI use, cheaters, and a KOS problem that makes DayZ look tame.

Latest Update: Nintendo reinstates SmileBasic 4 to the eShop after it was used for Switch 2 jailbreaks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (453 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
  • SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing owners to code their own simple programs and games.
  • Sources indicate that technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing owners to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Sources indicate that technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow owners to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

According to recent reports, nonetheless, Nintendo acted swiftly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to patch the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

Even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a newly introduced revision post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially rolled out, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

In a recent development, it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert debuted on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a significant hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

Industry observers note that the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it released. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

It has been revealed that this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

Sources indicate that if you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.
