  • According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains.
  • In any case, the update goes a tad further than that.

It has been revealed that A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 patch next week that adds in a fresh game plus mode.

According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

Overall, a bit of a smaller revision compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after one of the guitarists in Periphery had to leave their recent US tour two dates before the end, the vocalist decided to fill in one of the missing solo sections in a novel fashion. He learned it on the ocarina in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and rattled it out on-stage on the Switch 2, to a bewildered and captive audience.

Sources indicate that mark Holcomb, one of the group's three axe-wielders, posted footage of singer Spencer Sotelo's antics on Instagram. During 'Wildfire', Sotelo took out his trusty Switch 2, with Link primed and ready to shred, and belted through a truly unique version of the solo.

In a recent development, you can see he ain't miming either, both through his finger movements, and the fact the console is, indeed, wired up to the PA system. This is live entertainment, and the band is making the best of an unfortunate situation.

A post shared by Mark Holcomb (@markperiphery).

Only a couple of days prior, Misha Mansoor, another of the troupe's string-wielders, had to step away from the band's United States run due to a family emergency. Since there were only two shows left, the group decided to truck on as a four piece, with Holcomb, Sotelo, third guitarist Jake Bowen, and drummer Matt Halpern.

Recent findings suggest that periphery use backing tracks for their bass and synth parts anyway, so they could always just pipe in bits where Mansoor's contributions can't quite be covered by the remaining members. Otherwise, the ocarina is on hand for anything else.

Sources indicate that I should add, they do have a studio bassist, one Adam 'Nolly' Getgood, who helps produce their albums but stopped being a full-time member and touring back in 2017. Anyway, this little flurry of Nintendo-inspired instrumentation was performed at the last concert of the tour, when things typically get a little bit silly because everyone's excited to go home and rest.

It has been revealed that "This is the craziest shit ever," states one top comment. "Whole venue just got warped," reads another. They're certainly a band that'll keep you guessing.

In a recent development, if you're not too familiar with Periphery, imagine Meshuggah, Killswitch Engage, and Allan Holdsworth constantly having a scrap. You've got massive, dirty riffs, huge melodic sections, and offbeat, jazzy solos. Their latest full-length, A Pale White Dot, is a good starting point, but the conceptual double-album Juggernaut is their real magnum opus, in my view.

They had Ne Obliviscaris as main support for the bill on this tour, and if you've not listened to Portal of I, you should rectify that immediately. Greyhaven are there too, whose album Empty Black is a fine slab of metalcore, and Ando San is opening. He's an up-and-coming hip hop musician who uses similar riffing to Periphery, and has a penchant for earworms.

In a recent development, speaking of Meshuggah, Periphery will be supporting them on their 40th anniversary arena tour across Europe and Britain next year, with Vildhjarta kicking things off each night. No guarantees of Link making an appearance, but that'll be a mighty show nonetheless.

Death metal band refuses to let touring get in the way of WoW Forever, starts playing it during shows thanks to the Steam Deck.

In a recent development, anthony is an Irish entertainment and games journalist, now based in Glasgow. He previously served as Senior Anime Writer at Dexerto and News Editor at The Digital Fix, on top of providing work for Variety, IGN, Den of Geek, PC Gamer, and many more. Besides Studio Ghibli, horror movies, and The Muppets, he enjoys action-RPGs, heavy metal, and pro-wrestling. He interviewed Animal once, not that he won’t stop going on about it or anything.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a upcoming installment.
  • Sources indicate that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
  • Sources indicate that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a upcoming installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

Sources indicate that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

Sources indicate that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

In a recent development, 2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

Sources indicate that 4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Recent findings suggest that today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

  • In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
  • "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester stated of his decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the tech giant. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester stated of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My blueprint was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

It has been revealed that wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the tech giant in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox revealed a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Sources indicate that wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a latest studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Industry observers note that despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

In a recent development, paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server issue". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

FromSoftware never specified the exact matter impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

This isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

It has been revealed that when you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

Recent findings suggest that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis noted that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

It has been revealed that interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

In a recent development, unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just debuted on consoles, the tech giant may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the upcoming paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, world of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Like Rockslicer, an axe that lets you mine ore.

In a recent episode of the official WoW: Forever podcast, senior game designer Aidan Moon spoke a little on his design philosophies, and items that players are yet to see: "There's a lot that they have not seen that I'm very happy with and I think is a great direction for the game.".

Industry observers note that moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?'.

"That's because, when we say we're a fantasy-forward game, that means that before optimisation, before it being good, it needs to be flavourful, it needs to feel like it belongs in the world and that the stats are essentially a storytelling mechanism for items.".

Ultimately, Moon thinks that interesting items that are memorable are far better for the game than a purely optimal numbers upgrade: "I would rather there be an Ogre Loincloth in the game that people talk about and get upset over, than just another strength belt that people go 'oh, that's just the mail strength belt in the dungeon'.".

As for what we're yet to get to, Moon, laughing, remarks: "I've done some stupid stuff.

"There may be an item that is master looter BiS—I'll just put it that way … Maybe you get extra stats if your bags are completely full." Finally. An item for people who are allergic to inventory management! Me. I'm talking about myself. My bags are so full please send help.

  • To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • Industry observers note that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being stated, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just debuted into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be significant or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

Industry observers note that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a proposal laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons presently in the works, and a wealth of newly introduced additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging upcoming video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Recent findings suggest that season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is stated to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
  • The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.
  • It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a tech giant called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a tech giant called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

It has been revealed that game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce new voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

It has been revealed that "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

In a recent development, the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game rolled out. It adds an entirely latest region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

According to recent reports, in preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen notes that Sandfall Interactive simply made the RPG they wanted to exist.
  • It has been revealed that as the world moves into what will undoubtedly be this year's big award winner, GTA 6, fans of last year's record-breaking game of the year Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 got the sad news that Svedberg-Yen had departed Sandfall Interactive.
  • This news was confirmed in an interview with GamesBeat where Svedberg-Yen spoke about her experience making the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen notes that Sandfall Interactive simply made the RPG they wanted to exist.

It has been revealed that as the world moves into what will undoubtedly be this year's big award winner, GTA 6, fans of last year's record-breaking game of the year Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 got the sad news that Svedberg-Yen had departed Sandfall Interactive. The story she led for the title resulted in it winning Best Narrative – one of the 13 awards the game was nominated for at last year's edition of The Game Awards (the highest in the show's history) – so naturally it was a bit of a blow to the fans of the game knowing the next game presumably won't have her on board.

This news was confirmed in an interview with GamesBeat where Svedberg-Yen spoke about her experience making the game. As the "third person on the team" she notes that "It was always, from the very beginning, a narrative-focused game." She cites this as a reason the game turned out the way it did: "There was that consistency from the very beginning.".

When asked if there was something the team was aiming for with this approach, Svedberg-Yen states "We make the game that we want to play, the game we wish existed. We write the stories that interest us, that we find compelling. We write the characters that we find compelling. ".

In a recent development, and while "other people had to consider market-type things," she notes that all she had to was think "what would be an interesting premise. What are the philosophical and emotional places that you could dig into and explore? What are the things that resonate for me, having gone through my various life experiences?".

Sources indicate that clearly, this approach worked out pretty well for the game, and is testament for what a strong creative vision can do for a game. Which is naturally a lot easier for a smaller team who doesn't have to answer to a massive publisher or shareholders.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst notes, and that's despite the "Game Pass cannibalization.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin.
  • In a recent development, first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit.
  • I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page.

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

In a recent development, first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only confirmed this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

Recent findings suggest that the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Industry observers note that blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
  • It has been revealed that after days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has confirmed Huang's resignation as tech giant president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately.
  • Industry observers note that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

It has been revealed that after days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has confirmed Huang's resignation as tech giant president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

Industry observers note that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, states she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

Nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the tech giant: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a company-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Industry observers note that nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the firm's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss.
  • It has been revealed that tarnation!
  • As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

It has been revealed that tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Significant Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

According to recent reports, peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

#86284. Breaking: Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

Breaking: Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.
  • That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy.
  • This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

According to recent reports, if you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

For a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

Before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokori Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

Visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

Industry observers note that head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

Recent findings suggest that you'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

Industry observers note that after finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

When ready, head to Death Mountain.

The aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

It has been revealed that now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

According to recent reports, inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!).

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

According to recent reports, once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

After the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

To leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

Complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Substantial Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

Sources indicate that on the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

Head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

In a recent development, with both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.).

According to recent reports, when you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's at the moment blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

Sources indicate that if you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

With that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two upcoming items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

The tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next major patch, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Sources indicate that previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

Industry observers note that the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Fresh Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

Industry observers note that the release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

In a recent development, the first latest Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver substantial Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this patch is the latest Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

According to recent reports, the Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a latest Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

In a recent development, "I essentially wanna get rid of [best in slot gear (BiS)]. I think that BiS is not a good thing for a videogame that's supposed to be about roleplaying aspects of it—that's why I've introduced the creature subtype system (where things are more effective against [for example] murlocs), I've introduced a biome system.".

That's my worries solved, then! Moon also chimes in and notes that "Back in Season of Discovery, I think the biggest bags we could give you were 32 slots … now you can make 98-slot bags. I open the bag and my screen just [explodes].".

Sources indicate that the major hullabaloo from player communities seems to be this idea that we're just doing resistance gear again. Back in Vanilla WoW, you'd have to farm a bunch of specific elemental resistance gear for specific raids, and it's something that nobody quite like that much.

The way I see this being different, however, is that Moon is very specifically talking about a "theoretical BiS list". In other words, this biome and creature-matching only has to be completely aligned if you want to be maximally sweaty and pump the highest numbers you possibly can.

Recent findings suggest that it does not seem like this gear is mandatory, and I think the actual motivation behind it seems better. Trading off a ton of damage just to get crappy gear pieces so you can survive feels bad, but realising you have the perfect-shaped peg to put into a hole (stop giggling) actually sounds satisfying.

In a recent development, not that there won't be problems, but I would genuinely rather WoW: Forever try and experiment properly with its gear systems, instead of following the same formula that the main game's been trundling out for the past 20+ years. I am, bare minimum, willing to wait and see how it pans out.

To do this, you have to buy the game on the Xbox Store first, and then acquire Xbox Cloud Gaming time via one of two means - you either purchase time on the Xbox Store, or you get a subscription to Xbox Game Pass that includes a certain amount of time per-tier (and you can top it up later if you need to).

Here's the breakdown for all of those:.

It has been revealed that there is also the option to play "free with ads" using Xbox Cloud Gaming, but we haven't verified that it works with GTA 6 yet (although there's seemingly no reason why it wouldn't), and it only gives you 30 minutes of game time before it kicks you off. Some of GTA 6's missions can last longer than 30 minutes, so that's not really ideal.

Anyway, while we're still in the process of dusting off our Xbox One consoles and trying GTA 6 on there for ourselves, we thought we'd first share some impressions from Xbox fans across the web on what it's been like for them so far.

Let's take a look at what some Xbox One owners are saying about it:.

Overall, it seems like most people are enjoying their time with GTA 6 on Xbox One so far, although that's not to say there haven't been issues in some cases. The biggest complaints seem to be that some players think it looks "blurry" (while others don't really see a problem), and there are also a small number of reports that it appears to disconnect for no reason sometimes.

There's also a bit of worry that the servers might not be able to handle the load during "peak" hours, and considering we're only on the first day of GTA 6's official launch, it's hard to say how things are going to go in that regard.

Meanwhile, every other version of Xbox Cloud Gaming officially runs at up to 1080p and 12mbps bitrate.

Industry observers note that if you want any further feedback about playing GTA 6 on the Xbox One, we'll aim to get some "hands on" impressions to you ASAP. Based on these initial day one impressions though, it seems to be working fairly well right now.

Keep in mind that you obviously need a strong and consistent internet connection in order to play games via Xbox Cloud Gaming, otherwise you may experience heavy lag, disconnects and all sorts of other problems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam.
  • New turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

New turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

"We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input matter on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

Amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar issues, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

"Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we declared earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer unveils a latest launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

According to recent reports, valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

Recent findings suggest that "I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

This next enhancement has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Recent findings suggest that luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

Sources indicate that you’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a fresh sports festival for you to take part in.

Industry observers note that one newly introduced gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is at the moment being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

In a recent development, "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson mentioned in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

It has been revealed that "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

According to recent reports, inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Recent findings suggest that since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.
